newsitem.title: DENMARK: Poll shows Danish Social Democrats gaining support.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Danish Social Democrats gaining support.

text.p: Denmark's ruling Social Democrats are now more popular than at any time since the September 1994 elections that put them into power, according to a Gallup poll published on Sunday.

The survey, in the daily Berlingske Tidende newspaper, showed 33 percent of respondents saying that they would vote for Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen's party if an election were held now, compared to 28.3 percent in a poll last month.
The party won 34.6 percent of the vote in the 1994 general election. New elections are due by September 1998.

Sunday's poll showed Rasmussen's Radical Liberal coalition partners losing support, to 4.3 percent from 5.0 percent in May. But the main opposition Liberals and their Conservative allies also fell, to 28.0 percent from 28.6 and to 12.8 percent from 14.1.

Translated into seats in the 179-seat parliament the percentages would make the Social Democrats the largest single party, with 59 seats, but still dependent on coalition partners and the parliamentary far-left against the Conservative-Liberal alliance, with a combined 73 seats.
